rationale: The Latin anchors *fragorem edere* ("to produce a crashing sound"), *sonare* ("to sound"), and *crepare* ("to crack/rattle") all point firmly to an auditory sense — making a sudden loud noise — rather than physical destruction or violent movement. This aligns precisely with crash.v.07 ("make a sudden loud sound"), as illustrated by "the waves crashed on the shore," matching the acoustic emphasis of the Old English attestations in Beowulf and Exodus.
